qa.question: What is the IP address of the infected Windows client?
qa.evidence: Only internal host observed with sustained external beaconing (169 outbound connections to 72 distinct external IPs).

qa.question: What is the MAC address of the infected Windows client?
qa.evidence: Ethernet source address on packets from 10.6.13.133.

qa.question: What is the host name of the infected Windows client?
qa.evidence: DHCP option 12/81 (FQDN DESKTOP-5AVE44C.massfriction.com); also seen as a DNS self-registration query.

qa.question: What is the user account name from the infected Windows client?
qa.answer: Not determined -- requires Kerberos/SMB authentication log parsing, which this lightweight parser does not implement.

qa.question: What is the Active Directory domain and domain controller?
qa.evidence: LDAP SRV record queries (_ldap._tcp...massfriction.com) and direct DNS query for WIN-DQL4WFWJXQ4.massfriction.com.

qa.question: What C2 infrastructure did the infected host communicate with?
qa.answer: Two rotating C2 fronts, both proxied through Cloudflare: windows-msgas.com (typosquat of Windows telemetry domains; resolves to Cloudflare anycast IPs 104.21.16.1/104.21.80.1/104.21.64.1/104.21.96.1/104.21.112.1) and varying-rentals-calgary-predict.trycloudflare.com (an explicit Cloudflare Tunnel subdomain; resolves to 104.16.230.132/104.16.231.132). Both received periodic HTTP POST requests every ~30-90 seconds with randomized token-like URI paths and no User-Agent header -- a beaconing pattern consistent with a C2 implant using Cloudflare Tunnel to hide its true origin.
qa.evidence: http_file_download_aggregation / raw http.log.json request pattern; dns_query_aggregation_non_benign chunk.

qa.question: What is the likely initial access vector?
qa.answer: Not conclusively determined. hillcoweb.com and www.truglomedspa.com appear as one-off DNS lookups shortly before the beaconing begins and may be part of a malvertising/redirect chain, but this pipeline could not confirm a download event tied to them.
